`layout_bipartite()` is the stable computation boundary introduced in
ggbipartite 0.10.0. It validates and normalizes an input once. Layers and the
high-level plot composer then consume the same coordinates.

## Input dispatch

Matrix input is selected only by `is.matrix(data)`. It must be numeric and
have non-empty, unique row and column names. The `row`, `column`, and `weight`
arguments must remain `NULL`.

Data-frame input is interpreted as long data. `row`, `column`, and `weight`
must name three distinct columns; ggbipartite does not guess them. Repeated
row-column cells are errors unless an aggregation function is supplied through
`duplicate`.

Both forms use the same rules:

- IDs are converted to character and then compared exactly. Case and
  whitespace are not changed.
- Weights must be finite and non-negative.
- A zero cell means that no edge exists.
- A row or column whose total is zero is an error.
- Input order is preserved when no tree is supplied. A tree establishes tip
  order when it is supplied.
- Tree and data ID sets must agree by default. `unmatched_data = "drop"` and
  `unmatched_tree = "prune"` are explicit opt-ins.

`interaction = "abundance"` is the default. With
`interaction = "binary"`, each positive weight is treated as presence. The
mode is never inferred from the observed values.

## Stable object schema

A `bipartite_layout` is a named list with five stable components:

| Component | Stable content |
|---|---|
| `nodes` | `side`, `id`, `order`, size, box bounds, and centre coordinates |
| `interactions` | `edge_id`, row and column IDs, weight, and drawing coordinates |
| `tree_links` | side, ID, and connector endpoints |
| `params` | resolved mode, origins, gaps, scale, and side orders |
| `trees` | original tree, reconciled tree, and validated plotting geometry |

Abundance interactions contain four polygon vertices per edge. Binary
interactions contain one segment per edge, including `xend` and `yend`.
Metadata columns are prefixed with `row_` or `column_` before they are attached
to nodes and interactions, preventing them from replacing coordinate fields.

Fields used only while calculating the layout are not part of this contract.
Consumers should depend on the documented columns above rather than on list
printing or incidental column order.
